newsitem.title: USA: U.S. human rights official to visit Balkans.
newsitem.headline: U.S. human rights official to visit Balkans.

text.p: The U.S. State Department's human rights supremo, John Shattuck, will visit the Balkans this weekend in a fresh bid to persuade Serbs and Croats to hand over indicted war criminals, a spokesman said on Thursday.
"Shattuck is going to push the Serbs and the Croats on the fact that they have failed to comply with their Dayton commitments on war criminals and on war crimes," the spokesman, Nicholas Burns, said.
Lats November's Dayton peace accord required the warring parties in former Yugoslavia to arrest suspected war criminals and hand them over to an international tribunal in The Hague.
Burns said Shattuck, currently visiting the Hague tribunal, would travel on to former Yugoslavia in the next couple of days.
Shattuck, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour, was expected to visit Banja Luka and Sarajevo in Bosnia, as well as Belgrade and Zagreb.
Burns said Washington was "very disturbed" by reports that four Bosnian Serbs working as police officials in the Serb entity in Bosnia were indicted war criminals.

He said the U.S. charge d'affaires in Sarajevo, Michael Parmly, met on Wednesday with Momcilo Krajisnik, the Serb representative on the Bosnian presidency, and told him the four people should be fired and sent to the Hague for trial.
The Hague tribunal has indicted more than 70 people for atrocities committed in four years of ethnic warfare in former Yugoslavia, but few of them have been arrested.
